To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
both significant decrease in platelets count and thrombocytosis (≥30%) are associated with increased length of stay, morbidity, mortality, and hospital acquired pneumonia in pediatric population.
both ≥30% decrease (≥30% decrease in the number of platelets in the blood) and thrombocytocpenia (TP) were associated with increased mortality and longer length of stay (days in hospital).
a ≥30% decrease of platelet count and thrombocytosis, graded according to NCI- CTC, are prognostic risk markers for mortality, morbity and length of stay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the significant decrease in platelets, which was not reported in the pediatric population.
the development of a novel, noninvasive, and low-cost method for the diagnosis of acute kidney injury.
the development of new methods of treatment of patients with thrombocytosis and thrombocytogenic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both TP and a ≥30% decrease of platelet counts are independent risk markers for mortality, morbidiy, and LOS.
both TP and significant decrease of platelets are risk markers for mortality and morbidity.
both ≥30% decrease of platelets and thrombocytenea, graded according to NCI- CTC, are independent risk markers of mortality, morbidity and length of stay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a ≥30% decrease of platelet count is a risk marker for mortality and LOS, and TP is a risk marker also for morbidity.
both ≥30% decrease and TP are associated with mortality, morbidity (infections), and LOS, and that the former is a prognostication risk marker even in absence of TP.
the presence of thrombocytosis and a significant decrease in platelets (30%) are associated with higher mortality, morbidity and length of stay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a decrease in platelet counts by ≥30% should be considered as a significant risk factor for mortality, morbity, and length of ICU stay, even without the presence of thrombocytosis.
the NCI- CTC can also be used for grading of TP, and that a significant decrease in platelets, even in the presence of normal platelet counts, is a prognos- tic risk marker for mortality and LOS.
both thrombocypenia and a significant decrease in platelets are associated with higher mortality, morbidity and longer length of stay.
